subject: Social Habits
title: Listening and following instructions
objectives: Children will stop and listen when an adult speaks.
Children will follow simple one-step and two-step instructions.
content: Listening ears, following one instruction and following two instructions.
teachingActivities: Get down to the child’s level and use their name before an instruction; give one instruction at a time at first; use gestures with words; praise listening; keep your voice calm; use games such as Simon Says.
learnerActivities: Stop and look when called and follow one-step and two-step instructions.
assessment: Observe whether each child stops and looks when called and follows a one-step instruction.
expectedOutcomes: Stops and looks at the teacher when called.

lessons.title: Listening ears
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will stop, look and listen when an adult speaks.
successCriteria: Stops and looks at the teacher
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with friends and use kind words.
lessons.starter: Ring the bell and say "Stop, look and listen. Listening ears on."
teacherActivities: Show how to touch ears and look at the speaker.
Ring the bell and say a child’s name.
Play a sound game: listen for the bell and clap.
learnerActivities: Children touch their ears and look.
Child stops and looks at the teacher.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to touch ears and look at the speaker. Children: Children touch their ears and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Ring the bell and say a child’s name. Children: Child stops and looks at the teacher.
Step 3. Teacher: Play a sound game: listen for the bell and clap. Children: Children listen and clap.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Good listening." Children: Children smile.

practical.title: Listening game
practical.safety: Use a bell that is not too loud. Keep the volume gentle, especially for sensitive children.

differentiation.support: Get down to the child’s level and say their name first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the bell ringer.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do when we hear the bell?

lessons.conclusion: Sit quietly and listen to a gentle sound.
lessons.homeConnection: Get your child’s attention gently by name before you give an instruction.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stop, look and listen when an adult speaks" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Listening ears, listening ears, turn them on.

lessons.title: One instruction
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will follow a simple one-step instruction.
successCriteria: Waits for the instruction to finish
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with friends and use kind words.
lessons.starter: Say "Simon says touch your nose" and show how to do it.
teacherActivities: Give a one-step instruction such as "Clap your hands".
Give a one-step instruction with an object: "Put the ball in the basket."
Let a child give an instruction to the group.
learnerActivities: Child puts the ball in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give a one-step instruction such as "Clap your hands". Children: Children clap their hands.
Step 2. Teacher: Give a one-step instruction with an object: "Put the ball in the basket." Children: Child puts the ball in the basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Praise children who follow it. Children: Children smile.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child give an instruction to the group. Children: Child gives an instruction.

practical.title: Simon says
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and the actions simple and safe. Never punish a child who gets it wrong.

differentiation.support: Show the action while you say it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give an instruction to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Waits for the instruction to finish
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child one simple instruction at a time and praise them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow a simple one-step instruction" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Two instructions
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will follow two instructions in order.
successCriteria: Follows two instructions in order with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with friends and use kind words.
lessons.starter: Say "First jump, then clap" and do both slowly.
teacherActivities: Give a two-step instruction: "Pick up the ball and give it to a friend."
Say "First and then" as you act.
Give another two-step instruction with a different object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give a two-step instruction: "Pick up the ball and give it to a friend." Children: Child picks up and gives.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "First and then" as you act. Children: Children repeat first and then.
Step 3. Teacher: Give another two-step instruction with a different object. Children: Child follows both steps.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise the listening. Children: Children smile.

practical.title: Two steps
practical.safety: Keep steps safe and short and the floor clear. Go back to one step if a child finds two too hard.

differentiation.support: Give one step at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remember three steps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Do two actions together and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise two-step instructions at home during routines.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow two instructions in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Listening games
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play listening games that need careful attention.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with friends and use kind words.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play listening games with sounds."
teacherActivities: Play the drum fast and slow and let children move.
Stop the drum and say freeze.
Hide a bell and let children find it by listening.
learnerActivities: Children smile and clap and cheer.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the drum fast and slow and let children move. Children: Children move fast and slow.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop the drum and say freeze. Children: Children freeze like statues.
Step 3. Teacher: Hide a bell and let children find it by listening. Children: Child listens and points.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "You are good listeners." Children: Children smile and clap and cheer.

practical.title: Sounds and freeze
practical.safety: Keep the volume gentle and the floor clear. Offer ear protection or a quiet space to a sensitive child.

differentiation.support: Move with the child and freeze together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the drum player.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do when the drum stops?

lessons.homeConnection: Play freeze games at home with music.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play listening games that need careful attention" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 listening check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child listens and follows instructions.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with friends and use kind words.
lessons.starter: Sing the listening song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: bell, Simon Says and two steps.
At each station give instructions and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: bell, Simon Says and two steps. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station give instructions and watch. Children: Child follows with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Listening stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the volume gentle. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one-step instructions only.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to give instructions.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: stops and looks when called; follows one instruction; follows two instructions; listens in a group.

questions.question: What do we do when we are called?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep giving simple instructions at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child listens and follows instructions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
